summary: Pinned session transfered to standby during preemptive canary backfill leading to mixed-model responses and unexpected billing
description:
Issue summary: During a regional canary backfill (preemptive capacity warmup) tenant requests pinned to a specific model variant were partially redirected to standby nodes that did not preserve pin metadata. Impact: customers saw mixed-model outputs (tokenization/format deltas) and a transient billing spike because requests hit higher-cost standby variants. This affected interactive chat sessions for a subset of NovaChat users and caused confusion in their QA cohort runs.

Observed timeframe: 2025-11-04 09:10 - 2025-11-04 10:40 UTC in us-east region.

Expected: Prewarm/backfill should not reassign or migrate pinned cohort mappings until pin metadata and affinity tokens are carried to target pool, or should honor pin affinity and fall back gracefully.

Notes: Customer reports reproducible within their long-lived session tokens when traffic overlapped with our orchestrator's preemptive backfill window.
impact: Mixed-model outputs for ~120 user sessions, intermittent 5xx rate increase for pinned endpoints, and a billing spike (~12% more inference units for affected tenant over 90 minutes). Business impact: customer QA runs invalidated; potential SLA breach for latency/consistency during canary window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer pins tenant to redwood/gpt-medium-v2 via model_version pin header.
2) Trigger sustained traffic from pinned session while orchestrator runs scheduled preemptive backfill in us-east.
3) Observe session responses intermittently switching to the standby variant (higher-cost quantized build) and tokenization differences.
4) Check serving logs for cohort reassignment entries around backfill timestamp.
logs_excerpt:
edge-proxy[2025-11-04T09:13:02Z] INFO request-id=abc123 cohort_lookup=COHORT:tenant-42 pin_token=tok-9a8b missing_on_target=true -- orchestrator assigned backfill-target=node-standby-07
serving-runtime[2025-11-04T09:13:02Z] WARN model_variant=redwood/gpt-medium-v2-quantized tokenization_delta=+2 bytes request_id=abc123 -- emitting fallback-log
billing[2025-11-04T09:14:05Z] INFO tenant=NovaChat units_charged=452 expected_baseline=404
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: preemptive backfill job moved traffic to standby nodes without carrying cohort pin metadata (pin_token absent on target).
Telemetry shows orchestrator 'backfill-assign' path marks targets as warm but omits cohort-metadata copy when target state = 'standby'.

Edge logs show cohort_lookup succeeded on source but cohort token returned 'missing_on_target=true' for backfill target. Service mesh retry paths then routed to fallback variant under cost-tier ladder.
Reproduced in controlled staging by triggering scheduled backfill; confirmed cohort mapping not copied for nodes in 'standby' pool when prewarm job uses fast-path optimization.
Related PR (linked) contains a recent change to backfill fast-path that bypasses cohort metadata copy for speed; probable root cause.
comments: 2025-11-04 10:00 - Support (Asha Patel): Customer reported mixed outputs and asked if model pin guarantees were honored during prewarm. Raised to SRE and Eng.
2025-11-04 10:25 - SRE (Diego Moreno): Found backfill assignments where 'cohort_meta' was null on target. Correlating with orchestrator fast-path change from PR #1409.
2025-11-04 11:05 - Eng (Marta Liu): Reproduced in staging. Fast-path skips heavy metadata copy; will propose a patch to preserve minimal pin metadata for preemptive backfill targets.
2025-11-04 12:40 - Support (Asha Patel) to Customer: Provided temporary mitigation steps (session header override) and advised to pause scheduled QA runs for 2 hours while we remediate.

2025-11-05 08:30 - Eng (Marta Liu): Patch ready (orchestrator PR 1456) to ensure cohort pin fields are atomically copied for standby pool targets; adding unit test and integration scenario for canary/backfill windows.
resolution_notes:
Temporary workaround: Instructed NovaChat to set explicit request header 'x-redwood-disable-prewarm-backfill: true' for critical QA sessions to force affinity to original serving pool. Short-term fix: reverted fast-path optimization in orchestrator and applied PR #1456 to ensure cohort pin metadata is copied to backfill targets. Long-term: add invariant check in canary scheduler that asserts pin_metadata presence before cutover, and add an automated test to simulate pinned sessions during preemptive backfill.

Rollout plan: deploy patch to staging (complete), then progressive rollout to us-east canary (5% traffic) with monitoring on pin-cohort integrity and billing deltas. Full region rollout scheduled 2025-11-06 02:00 UTC after successful canary.

Post-incident actions: runbook update (confluence) to include prewarm metadata validation and add alert on 'missing_on_target' cohort lookups to avoid silent mixed-model responses. Customer credit request acknowledged; finance engagement ticket created (INT-2048) to calculate credit due to NovaChat.
next_steps: 1) Monitor canary in us-east for 24 hours after full rollout (owner: Diego Moreno).
2) Add integration test to orchestrator suite covering pinned-cohort backfill (owner: Marta Liu).
3) Update runbook and set an alert for missing_on_target cohort lookups (owner: SRE runbook team).
4) Coordinate billing reconciliation and customer credit (owner: CS Finance).
